subtopics.title: The Tangle of Factors That Hold Development Back

questions.question: The contrast between the mineral-rich, poor DRC and resource-bare, rich Singapore shows that:
options: Resources are not destiny — what matters is whether they are converted into broad development or captured by a few, the failure called the resource curse
Minerals prevent development
Small countries always develop faster
Resources guarantee wealth eventually

questions.question: Education is called the master key among development factors because:
options: It is the cheapest service to provide
Without skills, investment finds no workers and technology finds no users — every success story invested in education first
It replaces the need for energy and resources
It is the only factor governments control

questions.question: Colonial railway lines frustrate development today because they were built:
options: Too late to matter
With the wrong gauge
From mine to port rather than town to town, serving extraction instead of internal connection
Only in coastal countries

questions.question: The word the examiner wants for how the development factors operate is:
options: Sequential — each factor acts alone in turn
Random
Identical in every country
Interrelated — drought pulls education, education pulls skills, skills pull investment, and the chain loops back

questions.question: The apartheid spatial legacy still shapes development because:
options: Forced removals and homeland policy placed millions far from jobs on the worst land, and that geography outlives the laws that drew it
The homelands were given the best farmland
All spatial patterns reset in 1994
Commuting costs are equal across the country

questions.question: The pair of figures defining South Africa's core social challenge is:
options: Inflation at 10% and growth at 5%
A Gini coefficient near 0,63 and unemployment above 30 per cent — over 40 per cent among youth
Life expectancy of 80 and full employment
A Gini of 0,3 and unemployment of 5 per cent

questions.question: Load-shedding counts as a development issue, not merely an inconvenience, because:
options: It only affects wealthy suburbs
It reduces carbon emissions
It closes the spaza's fridge, the clinic's cold chain and the factory's shift, and deters job-creating investment
It increases electricity exports

questions.question: The balanced assessment CAPS expects of post-1994 South Africa is:
options: Nothing improved after 1994
All challenges were solved by 2010
Only the economy matters in the assessment
Enormous gains in services and social grants set against stubborn unemployment, inequality and institutional strain — both halves true

subtopics.title: Community-Based Development: Rural and Urban Approaches

questions.question: The core principles of community-based development are:
options: Participation, respect for local knowledge, appropriate technology, skills transfer and community ownership
Speed, scale, central planning and imported expertise
Minimum cost regardless of fit
Private profit and competition

questions.question: Working for Water delivers development and environment gains together by:
options: Building large dams in every catchment
Paying local teams to clear thirsty alien vegetation, returning water to streams while providing wages and training
Importing water from neighbouring countries
Relocating villages away from rivers

questions.question: Upgrading informal settlements in place is preferred to relocation because:
options: It requires no infrastructure
Relocation is more expensive in every case
Relocation breaks the job connections and social networks that keep poor households afloat
In-place upgrading avoids providing tenure

questions.question: The honest limitation of community-based development is that:
options: Communities never maintain projects
It always fails within a year
It works only in cities
Projects are small relative to national need, can be captured by local elites, and complement rather than replace state-scale delivery

questions.question: Acid mine drainage is the problem of:
options: Acidic, metal-laden water from abandoned Witwatersrand shafts seeping toward rivers — a bill arriving decades after the profits left
Acid rain damaging mine equipment
Chemical spills from working platinum mines only
Salt water entering coastal mines

questions.question: Environmental damage is called a 'loan against development' because:
options: Banks finance most pollution
Eroded soil, polluted water and degraded land subtract from future production — the damage is repaid with interest, mostly by the poor
Loans are needed to clean it up
It only affects future centuries

questions.question: Poverty itself degrades environments because:
options: Poor communities prefer degraded land
Environmental laws exempt poor areas
Households without electricity strip woodland for fuel and hungry herders overstock fragile range — closing the circle back to deeper poverty
Degradation only follows industrialisation

questions.question: Tools that pursue development without environmental destruction include:
options: Abolishing all mining and farming
Exporting waste to other countries
Ignoring impact assessments to speed up projects
Environmental impact assessments, mine rehabilitation obligations, protected areas earning tourism income, and the renewable energy build

questions.question: The earphone knot stands for:
options: The interrelated causes of poverty — pulling one wire tightens the knot somewhere else
Poor telecommunications in rural areas
The complexity of trade agreements
Tangled electricity supply lines

questions.question: In the family story, the eldest child leaving school to herd goats after the drought shows:
options: That herding pays better than matric
The resource wire pulling the education wire — one factor tightening another
That schools close during droughts
The energy wire acting alone

questions.question: 'It is never the rocks; it is what a country does with them' summarises:
options: The importance of geology in development
Why mining is always harmful
The resource curse — treasure captured by a few funds their fights while everyone else stays poor
The need for more mineral exploration

questions.question: The golden rule of the stoep approach is:
options: People maintain what is theirs — plan it, build it, own it
Big projects always beat small ones
Outside experts know best
Speed matters more than fit

questions.question: The Eastern Cape wool farmers' success came from:
options: Government buying their wool at fixed prices
Pooling small harvests and grading them properly, reaching buyers and prices no lone farmer could
Switching from wool to maize
Exporting directly without any organisation

questions.question: Crime fell along Khayelitsha's upgraded walkways because:
options: More police stations were built
The walkways were closed at night
Residents co-designed lighting and routes they actually walk — the people who walk the path know where the fear lives
The settlement was relocated

questions.question: The evaluation sentence to keep for community projects is:
options: They should replace all state programmes
They fail more often than they succeed
They work only with foreign funding
Powerful but small — community hands and state muscle are both needed, each doing what it does best

questions.question: Burning the roof beams to stay warm this winter stands for:
options: Development that eats its own environment — a loan from tomorrow repaid with interest
The high cost of firewood
Poor building standards
Seasonal energy shortages

questions.question: The 'cruel twist' about environmental bills is that:
options: They are paid by mining companies first
They land on the poor first — the shack settlement, not the golf estate, sits beside the mine dump and drinks from the brown river
They arrive only after a century
They are covered by insurance

questions.question: Overgrazed slopes washing into dams hurt development twice because:
options: Cattle prices fall and rise
Farmers must move to cities
The land loses its soil and the city loses water storage in one motion
Dams become tourist attractions

questions.question: The sentence that ties the whole term together is:
options: Growth first, cleanup later
Environment must always outrank jobs
Development requires no trade-offs
Meet today's needs without stealing from your grandchildren's — development that plans to still be standing when they arrive
